correctness.rationale: For M=G(8,3) with 16 vertices, 24 edges, the Abrams-style unordered two-particle discretized cubical complex has exactly 120 zero-,336 one-,228 two-cells. Reconstructed oriented boundaries ∂1(v,[a,b])={v,b}-{v,a} and the signed square formula; independently computed ∂1∂2=0, rank ∂1=119 and rank ∂2 mod3=208. Nine fundamental graph cycles each avoid a vertex and lift to cycles in configuration, proving dim H1≥9; rank-mod3 yields dim H1≤9, hence rational ranks H1=9,H2=20. The G-equivariant particle-sum map identifies H1 with graph H1, giving χ1=e(g)-v(g)+1; cellular Lefschetz gives χ2=t0-t1+t2-1+χ1. Independent adjacency-preserving networkx enumeration recovered 96 automorphisms and exactly the displayed ten element-order/trace signature multiplicities summing 96. Averaged traces yield the C8 invariant dims two in each positive degree and the full G quotient rationally acyclic. Suitable subdivision and rational finite-group quotient theorem are invoked standard theorems; computation is finite and fully enumerated for this graph.

value.rationale: A complete equivariant homology character under all 96 graph automorphisms is a natural, genuinely stronger invariant than Betti numbers. The contrast between C8 and full G rational quotient homology is a useful symmetry reduction; the graph is a canonical symmetric cubic graph rather than a cherry-picked finite set. Exhaustively computing a finite natural invariant can be valuable without yielding a universal graph theorem.

scientific_limitations: Only unordered distinct geometric points with n=2 on M=G(8,3), rational action and quotient homology.
No claim about integral torsion, local systems, or contractibility of quotients.
